units.translation: Often in the hospitable halls of my father
Often in troubles the helpless one
Often I fall with tattered garment
The surpassing strength of the earth and the heavenly pole on his shoulders
The surpassing strength of the earth and the heavenly pole on his shoulders
murderous cutting off of the head
with many men, full of men
having many men, crowded with men
And the impetuous lord of many-men'd Asia
with many men of the Greeks
And the impetuous lord of many-men'd Asia
around the woman with many husbands
around the woman with many husbands
For which of men did the gods so admire, and the city-sharing, much-nourishing lifetime of mortals –?

sic correcti pro πόλεως πολύβοτος τ᾽. Breviter schol. in M ὁ ὑπὸ πολλῶν ἐμβατευόμενος ἀνδρῶν, ἢ ὁ ἐπιπολὺ ἐκτεινόμενος, quarum interpretationum prior ad πολύβατος, altera ad πολύτατος spectare videtur. Scholiastae veteris annotationem suis additamentis auxit scholiasta Byzantinus ἁπλῶς πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι [simply all men] · τοῦτο γὰρ δηλοῖ τὸ “πολύ-βοτος αἰὼν βροτῶν, ἤγουν ἡ ζωὴ καὶ ὁ βίος τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ὁ πολύβοτος καὶ ὁ πολλοὺς τρέφων, ἢ ὑπὸ τῶν πολλῶν ἐμβατευόμενος ἢ ὁ ἐπὶ πολὺ ἐκτεινόμενος [for this is what “much-nourishing lifetime of mortals” means, that is the life and livelihood of men, the much-nourishing and the one feeding many, or the one frequented by many, or the one extending far]. Thomas Mag. ὁ πολύβοτος ἢ ἀντὶ τοῦ πολυκτήμων λογιστέον, ἢ ὁ πολλοὺς βό-σκων [“much-nourishing” is to be understood either as “rich in possessions” or as “feeding many”].
